v2Wbstate.title: v2Wbstate
v2Wbstate.description:
CHARGING - The socket is charging.

IDLE - The socket is idling.

READY_FOR_CHARGING - The socket is ready for charging.

RECOVER_FROM_ERROR - The socket is recovering from an error.

SERVICE_MODE - The socket is in service mode.

SUSPENDED - The socket is suspended.

TOKEN_PROGRAMMING_MODE - The socket is in RFID programming mode.

UNRECOVERABLE_ERROR - The socket is in an unrecoverable error state.

UNAVAILABLE - The socket is OUT OF ORDER as a result of change availability.

OFFLINE - The wallbox is not currently connected to the CPM.

DEGRADED - The wallbox has some error (see the errorCode).

profilePurpose.title: profilePurpose
profilePurpose.description:
Profile purpose

MAX_AVAILABLE_CURRENT - Only one profile of this type. It corresponds to the value of MaxAvailableCurrent.

CHARGE_POINT_EXTERNAL_CONSTRAINTS - From OCPP: Additional constraints that will be incorporated into a local power schedule.
                    Only valid for a Charging Station. From SYSTEM: from an external meter.

CHARGE_POINT_MAX_PROFILE - Configuration for the maximum power or current available for an entire Charging Station.

TX_DEFAULT_PROFILE - Default profile that can be configured in the Charging Station. When a new transaction is started,
                    this profile SHALL be used, unless it was a transaction that was started by a RequestStartTransactionRequest with an
                    ChargingProfile that is accepted by the Charging Station.

TX_PROFILE - Profile with constraints to be imposed by the Charging Station on the current transaction, or on a new
             transaction when this is started via a RequestStartTransactionRequest with a ChargingProfile. A profile with
             this purpose SHALL cease to be valid when the transaction terminates.

profileSource.title: profileSource
profileSource.description:
Profile source

SYSTEM - generated by the wallbox (internally). Can only be retrieved.

OCPP - all profiles are manageable via OCPP as well.

currentOffered.title: [mA] The current offered to the vehicle (corresponds to the PWM value)

temperature.title: [hundreths of a degree Celsius] 24,16 degrees will have the value 2416

v1Wbstate.title: v1Wbstate
v1Wbstate.description:
CHARGING - The socket is charging.

IDLE - The socket is idling.

READY_FOR_CHARGING - The socket is ready for charging.

RECOVER_FROM_ERROR - The socket is recovering from an error.

SERVICE_MODE - The socket is in service mode.

SUSPENDED - The socket is suspended.

TOKEN_PROGRAMMING_MODE - The socket is in RFID programming mode.

UNRECOVERABLE_ERROR - The socket is in an unrecoverable error state.

UNAVAILABLE - The socket is OUT OF ORDER as a result of change availability.

OFFLINE - The wallbox is not currently connected to the CPM.

DEGRADED - The wallbox has some error (see the errorCode).

v1SessionStatus.title: v1SessionStatus
v1SessionStatus.description:
Session status

INITIATED - Status set on creation of a new charging session.

PWM_CHARGING - status is for Mode3 sessions and is set when the EV is charging.

BLOCKED - The session is blocked (e.g. EV is open and no longer charging).

CLOSED - The state is set on charging session closing (at unplug or pre-authorization expiration).

terminationReason.title: terminationReason
terminationReason.description:
Termination reason

UNPLUG_EV - The session was terminated because the EV was unplugged.

SOCKET_FAILURE- The session has been terminated because of a socket failure (for
    example PERSISTENCE_ERROR or ERROR_RECOVERY)

LOCAL - Local cleanup of the session.

REMOTE - Remote operation has closed the session.

SOCKET_FW_UPDATE - The wallbox is going to reboot to update the firmware.

SOCKET_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT - The wallbox has not received a response to the heartbeat request within
    the request timeout period.

SOCKET_REBOOT - The wallbox is going to reboot.

POWER_LOSS - The chargepoint has suffered a power loss.

HARD_RESET - Hard reset.

SOFT_RESET - Soft reset

UNLOCK_CONNECTOR - Connector has been unlocked.

DE_AUTHORIZED - The session has been de-authorized (e.g. rejected StartTransactionReq).

USER_TERMINATED_RFID - user terminated with RFID card

USER_TERMINATED_SMARTHOME - user terminated with by smart home command

FORCE_CLOSE - Forcefully closed - used in IFS mechanism when session was not closed properly

tokenId.title: The Token.id that authorized the session

name.title: [required] Name is mandatory and must be unique

validFrom.title: Number of milliseconds since January 1, 1970, (UTC). If null validity starts now.

validTo.title: Number of milliseconds since January 1, 1970, (UTC). Can be null (never ending)

ocppId.title: ocppId must be unique. Otherwise any previous profile with this id will be removed

BLOCKED - The session is blocked (e.g. EV is open and no longer charging).

CLOSED - The state is set on charging session closing (at unplug or pre-authorization expiration).

SOCKET_REBOOT - The wallbox is going to reboot.

POWER_LOSS - The chargepoint has suffered a power loss.

HARD_RESET - Hard reset.

SOFT_RESET - Soft reset

UNLOCK_CONNECTOR - Connector has been unlocked.

DE_AUTHORIZED - The session has been de-authorized (e.g. rejected StartTransactionReq).

USER_TERMINATED_RFID - user terminated with RFID card

USER_TERMINATED_SMARTHOME - user terminated with by smart home command

USER_TERMINATED_PAYMENT_TERMINAL - user terminated by using the payment terminal
FORCE_CLOSE - Forcefully closed - used in IFS mechanism when session was not closed properly

The file needs to be in .pfx format and hold both private and public keys.
    You'll need to supply the password for the .pfx.
    Call /webui/https/enable upon a successfull install to start using the newly installed certificate.

    Args:
        query_args 'password' corresponding to the .pfx.
    Returns:
        responseMessage the result of the import operation.

    Example:
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -F 'files[]=@webui.pfx' --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/configs/webui/certificate/import?password=testpass
post.summary: Install the WebUI certificate.

    After triggering this endpoint you can follow the update progress with /upload/status.

    While the update is running, an updatelock is held.
    This can be checked by querying GET on /lock.
    When the update finishes, GET on /lock will return 404.

    If the updatelock is not removed after a period (consider up to 60 minutes),
    you should manually remove the lock by DELETE on /lock and then
    clean the repository by DELETE on /repository.

    Args:

    Return:
        ResponseMessage 200 indicating the result of the start operation
        ResponseMessage 400 if there's no .keb to start the update with

    Example:
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -X POST --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/updates/upload/start

post.description:
CPM contacts update portal, and returns synchronously the latest update information found at update portal.
    The information is being cached inside CPM update service and will be stored until periodic check task executes,
    new /portal/check POST or /portal DELETE requests are received.

    Args:
    Return:
        UpdateInfoResponse containing the json format of update information as returned by update portal.
        {
           "location":"https://127.0.0.1/ifconfig.keb",
           "retrieveDate":1641566534,
           "installDate":1641566534,
           "retries":10,
           "retryInterval":30,
           "description":"This is a ifconfig test .keb",
           "signingCertificate":"-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- ... -----END CERTIFICATE-----",
           "signature":"Rt58b..."
        }
        Location is mandatory and the rest of the fields are optional!

        It returns:
            204 if there are no updates available,
            404 if there is no update information,
            500 if any internal error appears

    Example:
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -X POST --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/updates/portal/check
post.summary: Get fresh update information from portal.

        file (str): The filename of the returned .csv.
            If not provided default is 'securitylogs.csv'
    Returns:
        .csv file. The response has the following headers:
                < content-type: text/csv; charset=utf-8
                < content-disposition: attachment; filename=securitylogs.csv
                < date: Sun, 21 Nov 2021 12:00:52 GMT
                < Transfer-Encoding: chunked

        ResponseMessage in case of failure

    Example:
        curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/securitylogs/export?file=securitylogs.csv

    Export .csv format:
        #Chargepoint: 19322483
        #Software version: 1.13.0
        #Exported on: 02-01-2022 16:48:56
        #Event;Critical;Timestamp;Tech info
        StartupOfTheDevice;true;20-12-2021 12:38:15;
        StartupOfTheDevice;true;02-01-2022 12:28:03;
        webUIPasswordChange;false;02-01-2022 16:40:19;extra info
get.summary: Export all Security Logs from the system into a .csv

get.description:
This is useful for paging the results with the same filters
    and then requesting one page at a time.

    Args:
        WallboxCountQuery holding the desired filters

    Returns:
        total the number of wallboxes conforming to the given filters
        responseMessage indicating the details of failure

    Example:
        Filters can be defined in the same way as the wallboxes retrieve endpoint.
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/wallboxes/count
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" '--insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/wallboxes/count?filters=STATE=IDLE'
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" '--insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/wallboxes/count?filters=STATE=IDLE&filters=NUMBER=1'
get.summary: Total number of Wallboxes that match the given filters.

        Example:
            curl --location --request POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/sessions/exportAsync?orderField=SESSION_START_DATE&orderDir=ASC&filters=SESSION_START_DATE=1639584106585'             --header 'Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN'

        Export .csv format:
            Charging Station ID;Serial;RFID Card;Status;Start;End;Duration;Meter at start (Wh);Meter at end (Wh);Consumption
            3;16350815;6666666;CLOSED;15-12-2021 16:01:46;15-12-2021 16:01:58;11 s;99;108;0.01 kWh

post.description:
This will trigger automatic retrieval and installation of a .keb file indicated
    at a given location (ftp, http/https).
    Status of the download and installation can be checked with /request/status endpoint.

    While the update is running, an updatelock is held.
    This can be checked by querying GET on /lock.
    When the update finishes, GET on /lock will return 404.

    If the updatelock is not removed after a period (consider up to 60 minutes),
    you should manually remove the lock by DELETE on /lock and then
    clean the repository  by DELETE on /repository.

    Args:
        location      : is mandatory and has to point to the given .keb (ftp/http/https sources).
        retrieveDate  : unix time - can be in the future. If it's in the past, retrieval starts immediately.
        installDate   : unix time - must be after retrieve date. If retrieve has not yet finished,
                            install will run immediately after retrieve finishes.
        retries       : number of retries to try and retrieve the .keb. Consider using a lot for bad networks.
        retryInterval : time between retries (sec)
    Only for signed updates:
        signingCertificate  : the public certificate used for signing the .keb update (.pem format)
        signature           : the signature of the .keb update

    Return:
        ResponseMessage indicating the result of the operation

    Example:
    Regular update:
        curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json"  -X POST --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/updates/request -d'{ "location" : "http://127.0.0.1/ifconfig.keb", "retrieveDate" : 1641566534, "installDate" : 1641566534, "retries" : 10, "retryInterval" : 30}'
    Signed update:
        curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json"  -X POST --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/updates/request -d'{ "location" : "http://127.0.0.1/ifconfig.keb", "retrieveDate" : 1641566534, "installDate" : 1641566534, "retries" : 10, "retryInterval" : 30, signingCertificate : "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- ... -----END CERTIFICATE-----", signature : "Rt58b..."}'

post.description:
The filename must have .keb extension.
    Note that this does not trigger the update.
    You'll have to do that through the dedicated endpoint /start after
    upload has successfully finished.
    You can follow the installation status with /status

    In case of a power-cut of the wallbox, the .keb file needs to be
    uploaded again in case it was only uploaded and not yet triggered.

    This operation could take a while, but it's being handled aynch so you can make
    other calls in parallel.

    Args:
        file that needs to be uploaded
    Returns:
        responseMessage the result of the import operation.

    Example:
        You'll need to supply the Content-Length and the Content-Type header with boundary:

        curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -X POST  -F 'files[]=@ifconfig.keb' --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/updates/upload
        *   Trying 127.0.0.1:8081...
        * TCP_NODELAY set
        * Connected to 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1) port 8081 (#0)
        > POST /updates/upload HTTP/1.1
        > Host: 127.0.0.1:8081
        > User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
        > Accept: */*
        > Content-Length: 1687
        > Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=------------------------07924f42de97ba6d
        > Expect: 100-continue
        >
        * Mark bundle as not supporting multiuse
        < HTTP/1.1 100
        < date: Fri, 07 Jan 2022 11:31:44 GMT
        * We are completely uploaded and fine
        * Mark bundle as not supporting multiuse
        < HTTP/1.1 200
        < content-type: application/json
        < content-length: 70
        < date: Fri, 07 Jan 2022 11:31:44 GMT
        <
        * Connection #0 to host 127.0.0.1 left intact
        {"acceptStatus":"ACCEPTED","msg":"Uploaded successfully","status":200}


        The body itself looks like this:

post.description:
The filename must have .keb extension.
    Note that this does not trigger the update.
    You'll have to do that through the dedicated endpoint /start after
    upload has successfully finished.
    You can follow the installation status with /status

    In case of a power-cut of the wallbox, the .keb file needs to be
    uploaded again in case it was only uploaded and not yet triggered.

    This operation could take a while, but it's being handled aynch so you can make
    other calls in parallel.

    Args:
        file that needs to be uploaded
    Returns:
        responseMessage the result of the import operation.

    Example:
        You'll need to supply the Content-Length and the Content-Type header

        curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -X POST --data-binary '@ifconfig.keb' --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/updates/upload

get.description:
This returns, immediately, the current update information cached inside CPM UpdateService,
    without contacting update portal. This information is refreshed by CPM every X days.

    Args:
    Return:
        UpdateInfoCacheResponse Containing the json format of update information if there is any cached update information.
        {
           "location":"https://127.0.0.1/ifconfig.keb",
           "retrieveDate":1641566534,
           "installDate":1641566534,
           "checkDate":1641566534,
           "retries":10,
           "retryInterval":30,
           "description":"This is a ifconfig test .keb",
           "signingCertificate":"-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- ... -----END CERTIFICATE-----",
           "signature":"Rt58b..."
        }
        Location is mandatory and the rest of the fields are optional!

        It returns 404 if there is no update information cached yet at CPM side.
    Example:
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/updates/portal

post.description:
This is designed to be used if we need to
    make a fresh access token for a user (by verifying they have the
    correct username and password).

    Unlike the standard login endpoint, this will only return
    a new access token (no refresh_token), so that we don't keep
    generating new refresh tokens, which entirely defeats their point.

    Args:
        LoginRequest both 'username' and 'password' must be provided
    Returns:
        LoginResponse response with a new 'access_token' (and no refresh_token -> use the one you already hold)
        ResponseMessage in case of failure to login

    Example:
        PASS=19326885
        curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST -d '{"username":"admin","password":"'$PASS'"}' --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/jwt/fresh-login

post.description:
This will generate a new access token from
    the refresh token, but will mark that access token as non-fresh,
    as we do not actually verify a password in this endpoint.

    Args:
        refresh_token 'Authorization: Bearer $REFRESH_TOKEN' must be provided in the HTTP headers
    Returns:
        LoginResponse response with a new 'access_token'
        ResponseMessage in case of failure

    Example:
    This will fail as we need to use the REFRESH_TOKEN and not the ACCESS_TOKEN
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -X POST --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/jwt/refresh

    This will work as we supply the refresh token
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REFRESH_TOKEN" -X POST --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/jwt/refresh
        This returns an access_token that is no longer fresh (some endpoints will require you to have a fresh access token)

post.description:
It is strongly recommended that these are removed from the client as soon as this endpoint is called.

    To access this endpoint you need to supply the access_token in the http header.
    In order to fully logout, you'll need to supply the refresh_token in the payload as well.
    Both tokens will be invalidated and you'll need a new standard login to get new ones.

    Args:
        access_token 'Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN' must be provided in the HTTP headers.
        LogoutRequest containing the refresh_token
    Returns:
        ResponseMessage indicating the result
    Example:
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST -d '{"refresh_token":"'$REFRESH_TOKEN'"}' --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/jwt/logout

post.description:
Will return a fresh access token and a refresh token.

    Args:
        LoginRequest both 'username' and 'password' must be provided
    Returns:
        LoginResponse response with both 'access_token' and 'refresh_token'
        ResponseMessage in case of failure to login

    Example:
    PASS=19326885
    LOGIN_INFO=`curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST -d '{"username":"admin","password":"'$PASS'"}' --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/jwt/login`
    ACCESS_TOKEN=`echo $LOGIN_INFO | awk -F '"' '{ print $4 }'`
    REFRESH_TOKEN=`echo $LOGIN_INFO | awk -F '"' '{ print $8 }'`

get.description:
Args:
        SessionQuery: criteria that matches the returned Sessions
    Returns:
        list json list of Session.
            Note that the result is automatically limited to 200 entries.
        responseMessage indicating the details of failure

    Example:
        Get latest 200 sessions (ordered by descending session start date)
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/sessions/

        Get next 10 sessions starting from the 5th result of all sessions in descending order by their session start date.
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" '--insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/sessions/?offset=5&limit=10&orderField=SESSION_START_DATE&orderDir=DESC'

        Get latest 10 sessions ordered by session start date descending that belong to the Wallbox with serial number 16350815
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" '--insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/sessions/?offset=0&limit=10&orderField=SESSION_START_DATE&orderDir=DESC&filters=SOCKET_SERIAL_NUMBER=16350815'

        Find latest Session authorized with a specific Token
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" '--insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/sessions/?offset=0&limit=1&orderField=SESSION_START_DATE&orderDir=DESC&filters=CHARGING_TOKEN_ID=4444444'

        Get all sessions in the given interval (intrinsec comparator for SESSION_START_DATE is '-gte' and for SESSION_END_DATE is '-lte')
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" '--insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/sessions/?filters=SESSION_START_DATE=1639569600000&filters=SESSION_END_DATE=1639584118101'
        Same action as above but using some UTC formatted dates (url encoded of 15-12-2021 14:00:00 to 15-12-2021 18:01:58):
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" '--insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/sessions/?filters=SESSION_START_DATE=15-12-2021%2014%3A00%3A00&filters=SESSION_END_DATE=15-12-2021%2018%3A01%3A58'

        Use comparators for fields: use one of: '-gt' '-gte' '-lt' '-lte' '-eq' after the field name
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" '--insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/sessions/?filters=SESSION_START_DATE-gt=1639569600000&filters=SESSION_END_DATE-lte=1639584118101'

        Use multiple filter occurences:
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" '--insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/sessions/?filters=SESSION_START_DATE-gt=1639569600000&filters=SESSION_START_DATE-lt=1639584118101'
get.summary: Return a list of Sessions which match the given filters.

        Use multiple filter occurences:

The RESTAPI version scheme has format Major.Minor.Patch (e.g. 1.0.0)
    Major versions have breaking changes in them and are not backward compatible.
        They are also indicated in the path (/v1 for 1.X.Y or /v2 for 2.X.Y).
    Minor versions are backward compatible throught the Major version. (1.2.0 will support all functions of 1.0.0).
        Note that some new fields could be added in a Minor version, but no fields are deleted or renamed.
    Patch versions only solve very specific problems and should not break the Minor version formatting.
        Expect this for non-functional changes (backend changes).

    Returns:
        version the current api version

    Example:
        curl --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/version

get.description:
This will trigger retrieval if necessary (MVA records are not yet synched).
    The retrieval (records synch) operation is done asynchronously.

    Before exporting the records, this endpoint must be called to ensure
    that all records have been synched (and thus are ready for export).

    As the synching of the records might take a while, after calling this
    you can check the status of the synch with the dedicated endpoint.

    Args:
        serialNumber: the serial number of the wallbox we want to export the records for
        type: the type of mva record (MEASUREMENT or LOG)
        list: optional list of specific records to retrieve. Format is: 1,3,5-8,20,50-101.
            Not specifying the list will retrieve all records of given type.

    Return:
        MvaResponse holding the process infromation
        ResponseMessage indicating any failure

    Example:
        Retrieve all LOG records
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/mvas/synch/19322483/LOG

        Retrieve records 1 and 5 through 10
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/mvas/synch/19322483/LOG?list=1,5-10

        Retrieve all MEASUREMENT records
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/mvas/synch/19322483/MEASUREMENT?list=1,5-10
